events.description: Arrest of Islamic extremist cell in Jordan and an Algerian in Canada smuggling explosives
Rocket attacks on US Embassy and American Center in Islamabad
Clinton trip to India, Bangladesh, Pakistan; reports of assassination targeting
Leaders of three extremist groups in Pakistan and Bangladesh signed Bin Ladin's anti-US fatwa, declaring intent to retaliate for any US attack on him.
President Clinton's trip to India, Bangladesh and Pakistan; reports that local Islamic extremists were targeting him for assassination.
Rocket attacks targeted the US Embassy and American Center in Islamabad.
Militants begin training in Afghan camps (since 1979).
Fall of Communist government in Afghanistan, followed by civil war creating a favorable environment for terrorists.
Arrest of Islamic extremist cell in Jordan.
Arrest of Algerian extremist, Ahmed Ressam, attempting to smuggle explosives into the US from Canada.
Hundreds of men were training in Afghanistan.
CIA Counterterrorist Center issues intelligence report on Afghanistan as an incubator for terrorism.

key_claims: Afghanistan under the Taliban hosts over two dozen training camps for international jihadists.
An estimated 15,000 to 20,000 fighters trained in Bin Ladin-supported camps since 1996.
Taliban will support terrorist groups as long as Mullah Omar's hardline faction dominates and the war continues.
Pakistan, as principal patron, has most leverage over the Taliban but faces domestic and logistical obstacles.
Taliban and Bin Ladin benefit from the Afghan narcotics network.
Warlords Sayyaf and Hikmatyar would likely court Bin Ladin if the Taliban collapsed.
